title: Ignore Font Attribute for Title

illustrates.quote: Ignore font attributes for titles of books, poems, plays, etc., that appear as a complete heading. Note: Font attributes are retained when titles of books, poems, plays, etc., are mentioned in the text.

blocks.features: Centered, italic serif poem title standing as a complete heading.
Centered, full-capitals author byline beneath the title, plain (non-italic, non-bold).

Left-aligned (not centered) opening line of the poem — part of the same decorative title-page unit as the title/byline above it. Whether this line is itself italicized in print is unconfirmed (see uncertain); it makes no difference to the braille either way, since 5.3.5 drops the attribute as part of the same 'complete heading' unit regardless.

print.notes: Title-page-style block: italic title, plain full-caps byline, then the poem's opening line, all one decorative 'complete heading' unit per 5.3.5.
print.surroundingText: Follows rule 5.3.5 directly, on printed page 5-4, immediately after Example 5-3.
print.printFeatures: Three centered/left lines, no border: italic title, plain caps byline, poem opening line (italic per run A, plain per run B — unconfirmed either way, see uncertain).

braille.notes: Six lines, margin 8 stripped. Lines 1, 3, 5 are full blank-cell (U+2800) filler lines bracketing/separating the title, byline, and quotation, kept as empty strings. Title (line 2, indent 13) and byline (line 4, indent 12, double-capital sign) both verified centered by the (40−len)//2 formula. No typeform indicator anywhere: the title's and poem line's italics, and the byline's full-caps styling, are all dropped as font attributes, per 5.3.5 — the capitalization itself is retained via ordinary UEB capital signs, not as a font attribute.

uncertain: Whether the poem's opening line ('How wisely Nature did decree,') is itself printed in italics is a genuine disagreement between the two runs (A: italic; B: plain) that pixel-level evidence was not obtained for. It has no effect on the braille (5.3.5 drops the attribute here regardless, as part of the same title+byline+quotation 'complete heading' unit), so it is left unresolved rather than asserted either way; `print.blocks[2].text` is kept plain (no *italic* markup) so this section's own gold-run.mjs comparison isn't skewed by an unconfirmed guess.
resolution: Braille (including all three blank filler lines) independently re-derived from .txt lines 3936-3941 (margin 8) and matches both runs byte-for-byte; both runs' own summaries agree on this file's line count and content. Heading level (1, centered) newly verified here directly against the measured indent using the (40−len)//2 formula for both the title (indent 13, len 13) and byline (indent 12, len 15) — not taken from either run's own 'level' field (A asserted level 1/heading, B left level null throughout the section). Whether the poem's opening line is italic in print (A: italic; B: plain) is left as a documented uncertainty, not picked either way — see `uncertain`.
